newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Coffee catches brisk plays, cocoa vols up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Coffee catches brisk plays, cocoa vols up.

text.p: Interest picked up in coffee options on Friday after $1,350 March puts triggered a chain of activity.
Rising premiums reflected a friendlier view in the cocoa options market.
"Today was the busiest day on coffee for quite a while," said one floor trader.
The session saw a total 1,478 lots of robusta options changing hands but the volume was swelled by volatility trades to match an early buying interest on March $1,350 puts.

Sellers of the put also bought the March $1,350 call, creating a synthetic short position on the futures. The $21-22 premium gained on the put could then enable the player to lock in a profit by buying the March futures below $1,372.
Some also legged the March $1,200 put to the deal.
Volatilities remained mostly static this week in line futures relcutance to break free from the $1,415-$1,476 range basis January in the short-term.
But March $1,350 puts traded at a slightly higher 25-26 percent compared with 23-25 March strikes commanded earlier this week. January positions were stable at around 27-30 percent.
Futures traders expect robusta to remain under pressure from Asian and African origins but the downside risk is somewhat cushioned by roaster buying at the lows.
Attentions have turned to Friday's U.S. green coffee inventory for October which traders said could set the trend in New York and possibly London next week.
In cocoa, interest re-emerged on out-of-the-money calls and volatilities crawled up as the view that futures could have bottomed out at 910 stg basis March began to appeal.
But the overall volume was thin.
"Volatilies have started to increase but are they are still cheap," said one market maker. Under the spotlight was March calls which traded from 16 percent to up to 22 volatility.
March 1,000 calls commanded a premium of 10-15 stg which market makers said was a good bet.
Cocoa futures bounced on Thursday and Friday and March surfaced above a rigid downtrend channel for the first time in one month. It rose to 931 stg, but then quickly retreated.
Traders expect the market to remain vulnerable to increasing supply, especially from West Africa where shipments are speeding up. Upside chances could improve if March secured a close above 942 stg.
Volatility hunters were offering puts but demand was sparse.
A recommended strategy for longs was to buy the May 900 put and sell the 1,050 call at level, putting a floor and a ceiling to the market. Traders said this strategy also worked on the opposite side.
No fireworks were expected from December's expiry on Wednesday with no significant strikes around present market levels.
"December will go out with a bit of a whimper," said one.
In coffee, this week's trades also featured a calendar call spread on January and March $1,500.
A butterfly on January involved buying the $1,350 and $1,450 puts and selling twice the $1,400 put at a price of $7.
"It is quite a good strategy if you think the market will remain rangebound," said one market maker.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
